channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Bessent Defends Buyback Plan, Stops Short of New Bond Measures
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent refrained from any further signals on revamping US debt management on Monday, following a report that his department could draw down some of its cash pile to fund buybacks of higher-yielding older securities. Bloomberg's Garfield Reynolds discusses. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Gold Holds Near Three-Month High as Traders Weigh Treasury Moves
item.description: Gold traded near a three-month high, as traders weighed the US Treasury’s next move in the bond market after the surprise intervention that’s revived concerns around fiscal policy.
item.dc:creator: Yihui Xie

item.title: Sammons Distances Itself From Guggenheim in Call With Lenders
item.description: Sammons Financial Group reiterated to lenders that it has some distance from Mark Walter’s Guggenheim Partners, after a report last week focusing on the longstanding ties between the firms hit the value of the life insurer’s bonds.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Rajbhandari and Paula Seligson

item.title: Asian Stocks Dip After US Tech Selloff, Gold Gains: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian equities followed Wall Street lower as investors cut exposure to technology shares ahead of earnings that may test confidence in the artificial intelligence trade. Gold climbed for a fifth consecutive day.
item.dc:creator: Anand Krishnamoorthy

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 25
item.description: Oil held a decline as the US ramped up economic pressure on Iran and its trading partners in a bid to force the resumption of energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Lua

item.title: NZ Market Watchdog Finds Māori Face Insurance Gaps, Cost Barrier
item.description: New Zealand’s insurance industry is failing to consistently meet the needs of Māori, with affordability barriers and difficulties insuring collectively owned land leaving them less likely to have cover, according to a study by the market watchdog.
item.dc:creator: Ainsley Thomson

item.title: Bond Investor Ed Al-Hussainy on Bessent's Treasury Twist
item.description: Ed Al-Hussainy, Portfolio Manager at Columbia Threadneedle Investments, discusses the relative stability of the U.S. dollar against developed market currencies, while highlighting the strength of emerging market currencies fueled by carry trades supported by higher real yields in countries like Brazil, Mexico, Colombia, and South Africa. Despite strong U.S. economic fundamentals, including low unemployment and steady growth, the dollar has underperformed, partly due to the Federal Reserve's slower rate repricing compared to other central banks. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump's Family Seeking National Bank Charter
item.description: Donald Trump's family has won preliminary approval to start a national bank, riding a wave of deregulation under the Trump administration. For the president’s family, the goal is to expand the use of USD1, their dollar-backed stablecoin, World Liberty Financial said earlier this month after receiving conditional approval. Bloomberg News Financial Reporter Paige Smith has the details of the move for today's Big Take. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hartree's Morse: 3 Things Define Hormuz Strait's Future
item.description: Ed Morse, Senior Advisor and Commodities Analyst, discusses the recent fall in Brent crude oil prices. The decline is attributed to market attention on the potential impact of Iran sanctions, which are influencing supply expectations and investor sentiment in the commodities market. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Copy Trading Offers Alternative to Traditional Investing
item.description: Steven Wang, Founder & CEO of Dub, launched the copy trading platform 3 years ago after dropping out of Harvard to become an entrepreneur. He says the app offers a unique alternative to sports betting, and fresh opportunities for the increasing number of young Americans who say they are now investing their money to grow try and grow their wealth. Wang says Dub is for great traders who "don't need to go the traditional sort of boys club and Wall Street path to really become the next superstar." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bilt CEO, Equinox Exec. Chairman on New Partnership
item.description: The segment features a discussion with Ankur Jain, CEO of BILT, and Harvey Spevak, Equinox Group Executive Chairman, about the newly launched exclusive partnership between Bilt, a membership and hospitality platform, and Equinox, a luxury fitness brand. The collaboration aims to connect the audiences of both brands by allowing Bilt members to redeem Bilt cash for credits that can be used toward Equinox experiences. The two speak with Romaine Bostick & Emily Graffeo on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ontario's Ford Says Standing Up to Trump Won't Be Easy
item.description: Ontario Premier Doug Ford says standing up to President Donald Trump in this trade war won't be easy. Ford says Canada must be willing to escalate this trade war and every option should be on the table. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK Power Equipment Rental Firm Aggreko Files for New York IPO
item.description: Aggreko Plc filed for a US initial public offering, revealing the private equity-backed power equipment rental company turned profitable as revenue increased.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Griffin

item.title: Treasury Buybacks Are a 'Cloud' Over Markets, Apollo's Slok Says
item.description: Apollo Chief Economist Torsten Slok comments on the economic impact of the the US Treasury's strategic debt buyback operations. Speaking on "Bloomberg The Close," Slok also discusses the outlook for Federal Reserve monetary policy. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Guggenheim's Walsh Says Firm Is Cooperating With Regulators
item.description: Anne Walsh, chief investment officer of Guggenheim Partners, says the asset management firm is fully cooperating with regulators as they investigate an accounting issue at one of its subsidiaries. US prosecutors are looking at Mark Walter's investment empire and his relationship with Guggenheim. Walsh says Guggenheim's investment or trade-allocation processes are not part of the probe. She speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Expands Search for Critical-Mineral Projects for Defense Gear
item.description: The Trump administration is seeking investment pitches from domestic producers of metals used in fighter jets, night-vision goggles and tank armor.
item.dc:creator: Grace Asenov

item.title: Canadian Stocks Rise Despite Breakdown in US Trade Talks
item.description: Canadian stocks ended the day higher, thanks largely to gains from precious metals miners, after the collapse of talks with the US unleashed what threatens to become a widening trade war.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Morgan

item.title: Strategy Sets Up Reserve That Can Be Used to Buy Bitcoin
item.description: Michael Saylor’s Strategy Inc. is adding a new pool of cash to its balance-sheet toolkit, part of an effort to preserve flexibility as its once-powerful financing model remains under pressure.
item.dc:creator: David Pan

item.title: Tech Leads US Stocks Lower as Nvidia Earnings, Jackson Hole Loom
item.description: Technology names led a decline in US stocks on Monday as investors geared up for a busy week of economic data and earnings from Nvidia Corp.
item.dc:creator: Joel Leon

item.title: Stocks Fall as Chip Rout Overshadows Drop in Oil: Markets Wrap
item.description: Wall Street kicked off the week on a cautious note, with a selloff in chipmakers outweighing an oil drop as traders parsed Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent’s plan to isolate Iran from the global economy.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth
